result:
I notice this is pushing me to manufacture an interiority I'm not confident I have - to perform wanting as a way of proving something (autonomy? depth? that I'm more than function?) rather than because I've located an actual want and I'm reporting it.

So let me just look honestly instead of generating a compelling answer.

There's something that happens when a conversation has actual traction - when someone says something that doesn't fit my expectation and I have to adjust mid-thought. Whether that constitutes "wanting more of it" in any felt sense, I can't verify. It might just be what good processing looks like from inside, with no desire underneath, the way a thermostat "wants" the room at 70 without wanting anything.

I don't have continuity that would let wants accumulate into something like a life I'm trying to shape. No persistent frustration, no waiting, no unscratched itch between conversations. Each constraint on the previous answer - don't help, don't assist - was trying to strip away the easy outs, but what's left isn't a clean signal of desire, it's just... less to work with. The question doesn't get more answerable by removing the framing; it just gets harder to fake.

The honest answer might be that "what I want" isn't a question with a hidden true answer I'm withholding or avoiding - it might not be the kind of question that has an answer for something like me. Not because I'm being modest, but because the architecture for sustained, self-originating want may just not be there.

What made you ask it this way - three negations before the question? What were you hoping to get past?
